title: Eight CI guards grade NOTHING and eleven more are silently narrowed — and three of the dead are named in the #1 doc as live enforcing mechanisms
note: MEASURED by the E20 lane 2026-09-22 over a STATED POPULATION of 95 guard scripts — scripts/ci/check_*.py PLUS scripts/check_*.py, because check_claim_basis.py, the one CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL leans on hardest, lives in the latter. Every module-level repo-path constant tested with `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>`. Four states, never collapsed: live 30 · degraded 11 · DEAD 8 · no_declared_subject 46 (the instrument cannot speak to those, and it is the LARGEST bucket, so folding it into `live` would be this tool committing the defect it exists to find). [!] THE EIGHT DEAD: check_backlog_unresolve, check_claim_basis, check_open_items, check_operator_owed, check_recurrence_ledger, check_register_field_loss, check_soak_registered, check_stated_population. Every one is the 2026-09-21 reset's blast radius — it archived the four review backlogs, OPEN-ITEMS.json, the lease, SESSIONS.json, MERGE-QUEUE.json, session-board.json, RECURRENCE-LEDGER.json and operator-owed-register.json, and nothing swept the guards that read them. [!] AND THREE ARE NAMED IN docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md AS LIVE MECHANISMS, which is why this is not housekeeping: § Backlog governance says the status enum is 'enforced whole-file over every review backlog by claim-basis-guard'; § 'A soak must carry its own alarm' says check_soak_registered fails when a *_soak.jsonl exists with no register alarm; § Session-end reconciliation says operator-owed-guard fails on an item carried across commits without a state change. All three subjects are archived. A canonical doc naming a mechanism that cannot run is the folklore failure that document has its own section about. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: RE-POINT THE THREE NAMED ONES, RETIRE THE OTHER FIVE with stated reasons, and correct the doc text to match — the doc follows the decision, it does not lead it. [!] DO NOT PROMOTE THE 19 INTO A HARD FAILURE as part of this. E20 already wired scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py REPORT-FIRST, with a dated shrink-only baseline and counts printed every run; only a NEW dead or degraded guard fails. Keep that shape and let the baseline shrink by eight. resolution_criteria: the three re-pointed guards each FAIL on a planted violation against their new subject (a green re-point proves nothing); the five retirements each carry a written reason; CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL no longer claims a mechanism that cannot run; and check_guard_liveness's baseline is smaller by eight with the count visible in the diff. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-22 — PR #12756 MERGED, and `done` rather than `landed_unproven` because all four resolution criteria were RE-CHECKED ON MAIN after the merge (main 8a0669284), not inferred from the merge: (1) the re-pointed guards each FAIL on a violation planted against their new subject — self-tests 11/16/14/11 controls, run on main; (2) the four retired scripts are absent from the tree and each carries its reason in docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/guards/RETIRED-GUARDS-2026-09-22.md; (3) the only surviving mentions of the archived registers in CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL are inside the dated correction notes (lines 640, 1683), i.e. history, not a live mechanism claim; (4) guard-liveness reads dead 0, baseline 11 of 11, exit 0. [!] FOUR guards were re-pointed, not three: a manager addendum added check_allow_degraded, which was UNSATISFIABLE — 0 of 753 open PIPELINE rows were citable because check_backlog_refs.REF does not match a PI- id at all. [!] AND THE FIFTH RETIREMENT DID NOT HAPPEN: check_stated_population is NOT dead (verified by running it against a planted diff, exit 1); its population is a glob the liveness instrument cannot see, so 1 of 8 dead verdicts (12.5%) was a false positive. Retiring it would have removed the only mechanical floor under § 'Always state the population'. 8 findings filed in PIPELINE.jsonl.
